options.text: $(10p+q)-(10q+p)=9(p-q)$, so the difference of the number and its reverse is a multiple of $9$.
The difference is a multiple of $9$ even if $10p+q$ and $10q+p$ are read as products of letters, not place-value numbers.
The same place-value difference settles successive percentage discounts on a price.
Digits $p$ and $q$ as letters multiply to give the two-digit number.

stem:
Anaya writes a two-digit number as $10p+q$ and the number with its digits reversed as $10q+p$, with digits $p\neq q$.

Which claim correctly justifies a divisibility fact with place value?

teacher.key_rationale: Place value gives (10p+q)-(10q+p)=9(p-q), a multiple of 9 when p and q are digits.
